summary: Steel observation tower built on Bolton Mountain in 1921-22 by Ralph Dunsmoor; reported 30 feet high in September 1921 and 40 feet tall in July 1922 (materials for the tower); the Forest Lookouts entry ends with Removed and firelookout.org lists the site as gone.

facts.design: Steel observation tower, called a steel windmill tower in the January 1922 report
facts.status_note: The Forest Lookouts entry ends with the word Removed, with no date; firelookout.org lists the tower as gone.

events.note: Ralph Dunsmoor building the tower on the summit; reported as 30 feet high in September 1921

Steel tower erected on the summit, donated by C.D. Ordway and largely built by Ralph Dunsmoor; the January 1922 report says the cost was shared by the state club, the Burlington section of the Green Mountain Club, the state forestry department and private donations

corrections.why: Sources describe a steel windmill tower and a 40-foot steel observation tower, and firelookout.org lists an Open Tower. None of the sources describe a platform.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A September 1921 report gives 30 feet while the tower was still being built. A July 1922 report describes materials for a 40-foot steel observation tower being hauled to the summit; it does not give a finished height. The story gives each figure with its date and does not state a finished height. The record's 12.2 m comes from the 40-foot figure and is not confirmed as the finished height.

sources.title: 14 Fire Towers to Climb in Vermont
Watching from above: The story of Vermont's fire towers

notes_for_editor: Only the Forest Lookouts page describes this 1921-22 tower in detail, and it gives no removal date. UVM Digital Collections has 1921 lantern slides of a 30-ft steel tower on Bolton Mountain; these appeared only in search results, were not fetched, and are not cited. Whether the Vista Peak tower at Bolton Valley Resort (record us-vt-bolton, a separate entry) occupies the same summit is unknown; the editor may want to cross-link or merge the two. No source found describes the summit today or public access to it.
